What it measures: Does the video teach the lesson truly? Scored as the four sub-scores below, which are reported individually in the sheet — a single holistic number is what let r2's teaching scores compress to 95% of max with a 5-point spread across 37 videos. Weighted heaviest because the narration spine is the one thing edits can't manufacture.
What we can do: Re-roll. A weak spine can't be repaired; a strong spine makes everything else patchable.

What it measures: Every teaching beat of the lesson reaches the viewer. A beat the lesson spends a paragraph on and the video spends a clause on is partial coverage, not full.
What we can do: Re-roll, or graft the missing beat from a donor roll that covers it.

What it measures: The video uses the lesson's analogies, numbers, examples and order — not substitutes the engine preferred. A correct explanation built from material we didn't write still costs points here: the video is meant to substitute for THIS lesson.
What we can do: Re-roll with the beat named explicitly in the prompt; describe-don't-reference for illustrations.

What it measures: The why lands. A viewer could explain the idea back in their own words, not just repeat the sentence. Recitation of correct lines with no explanatory work is the middle of this band, not the top.
What we can do: Re-roll. This is the sub-score that most often separates two rolls of the same kit.

What it measures: Whether each kit board's points get taught, not whether the jpg appears pixel-exact. A board that never shows costs nothing if its content is fully covered (canon: why-learn-ai's everyday-apps board redrawn as 5 scenes = no deduction). Exact display is still the reliable way to score full marks; prompts still demand it. Absorbs r2's standalone Board fidelity dimension, which sat at 98% of max with a 2-point spread and never decided anything.
What we can do: Insert the board ourselves to match the narration (re-walk from kit jpgs).

What it measures: Gibberish/pseudo-text costs points only on content-carrying visuals (garbled label on a teaching chart); incidental b-roll props are forgiven. Also legibility, text containment, and white-on-light (hard visual fail, graded BAD even in transitions).
What we can do: Patch visuals: clone-freeze, graft, or masked restore (drawbox over invented figures). NOTE: these repairs usually spend pacing to buy cleanliness (the two dimensions correlated -0.47 across the r2 catalog) — score both after a repair, never just the one you were fixing.

What it measures: ALLOCATION and flow. Total runtime is NOT scored: a lesson with more to teach should produce a longer video, and one that earns its length takes full marks here. The minute range in Prompts/ is generation steering, not a grading standard (see GRADER-r3.md, 'Grade against THIS file, never against the prompt'). What is scored is whether the time budget is spent where the LESSON puts its weight. This stays distinct from Coverage: Coverage asks whether every beat reached the viewer at all; Pacing asks whether the proportions match. A video can land every beat and still spend 60% of itself on the opening anecdote while rattling through the four core moves - nothing missing, but the shape lies about what matters, and that is charged here. Charged both directions: dwelling past a beat's content, and rushing a beat the lesson dwells on. Plus flow: no padding with material the lesson does not contain, no final-scene starvation. DEAD TIME RULE (unchanged): a still frame costs nothing while the narration is still walking what's on screen; it costs once the narration has moved past it. A board held because each of its rows is being narrated is the lesson working as designed and is free. A 47s dwell that outlasts its own content, or a 100s pan across one illustration, is dead time and is charged here.
What we can do: Re-roll if the shape is wrong throughout. Otherwise: trim the over-served beat, graft donor motion over a dead span, or bring the next board in earlier. Read sections.txt in the grading bundle before scoring this dimension - it gives seconds-per-beat against the lesson's own word weighting.

What it measures: Missing a hard lesson requirement in the narration disqualifies a roll as spine (e.g. document-trap must say "Retrieval-Augmented Generation" in full; required verbatim lines).
What we can do: Nearly unfixable — the one true roll-killer. A cross-roll audio graft can occasionally rescue it when another roll speaks the line (support-trap 7/24).

What it measures: Profanity legible on screen, depiction of a real person against a by-name ban, or banned imagery classes (self-harm, medical, red-staining where fenced). Costs nothing against the roll's score but must NEVER reach students — this is a course for 16-year-olds.
What we can do: Patch or replace every violating span before ship; read every legible text span at full resolution during mapping.

What it measures: Getty/watermarked stock can never ship regardless of score (unlicensed; cropping the watermark is worse, not better). Engine-generated photoreal spans are a STYLE call, not stock — flag once, waivable. The lesson's own illustrations (repo assets from illustrations/ or lessons/) shown in-video are NEVER a violation of any kind (owner rule 2026-07-24).
What we can do: Insert illustrations, graft an alternative scene, or delete the span.

What it measures: Ships only ending on the close board as the literal final frame: no outro, no engine-drawn sign restating the message (named banned class).
What we can do: Insert our own close board over the final narration (freeze finisher / composed close).

What it measures: A/V sync: elements appear as narration mentions them; narration leads, visuals follow.
What we can do: Edit to sync: visual-replace over the untouched narration.

What it measures: A video enters the top teaching band only if a student could watch it INSTEAD of reading the lesson and lose nothing. "Covered the concepts" is the middle of the band, not the top.

Dimension: Scoring rule: cite or don't deduct
What it measures: Every deduction cites evidence (timestamp or quote). Every full mark states what WOULD have cost a point. A grader who can supply neither hasn't graded — this is the discipline that keeps a dimension from drifting to 95% of max.

Dimension: Scoring rule: one sitting per comparison
What it measures: Any claim that one batch of videos beats another requires those videos scored in the same sitting. Cross-sitting comparisons carry grader drift that looks exactly like a real quality difference (the 7/24 Avoid Traps animation step could not be cleanly attributed for this reason).

DECOMMISSIONED in r3 — do not reinstate. r2 scored "animation vs images" at 15 points; measured by variance it was effectively 35% of the grade while teaching was 20%, because animation was the widest-spreading dimension in the rubric (69% of max, 6-point range) and teaching the narrowest that mattered. It also double-counted pacing's dead-spot clause, and it charged videos for narrated board holds — i.e. for teaching well (canon: how-ai-answers, animation 7 with teaching 45/45, the best teaching score in the catalog). The legitimate half of it is now the dead-time rule under Pacing and attention. Motion is still nice to have; it is no longer scored.
Dotted paper, paper-craft, live-action hands, off-palette colors are tolerated; mention at most as one-line color in intake reports.
David can waive specific violations after watching; note waivers in the report and the sheet's Reason cell.
